title: Short Encoding of Words
prompt:
A valid encoding of an array of `words` is any reference string `s` and array of indices `indices` such that: `s` ends with the `'#'` character, and for each index `indices[i]`, the substring of `s` starting at `indices[i]` and up to (but not including) the next `'#'` character equals `words[i]`.

Given an array of distinct strings `words`, return the length of the shortest reference string `s` possible for any valid encoding of `words`.

examples.explanation: A valid encoding is s = "time#bell#" with indices = [0,2,5]. "time#" starts at index 0, "me#" (a suffix of "time#") starts at index 2, "bell#" starts at index 5.
A valid encoding is s = "t#" with indices = [0].

constraints: words[i] consists of only lowercase letters
hints: A word only needs its own entry in the encoding if it isn't already a suffix of some other (longer) word in the list — suffixes can be 'absorbed' for free.

Reverse every word and insert the reversed strings into a trie; a word being absorbable as a suffix of another word corresponds exactly to its reversed form being a strict prefix of another reversed word in the trie.

After building the trie of reversed words, only words whose reversed trie node is a LEAF (no children) need to be counted in the answer — for each such word, add its length plus 1 (for the '#') to the total.

solution.approach: Reverse every word and insert the reversed strings into a trie. A word W is a suffix of another word V exactly when reverse(W) is a prefix of reverse(V), which in the trie means reverse(W)'s end node has further children extending it (i.e. is not a leaf). So only words whose reversed trie node ends at a leaf (no children below it) actually need their own separate entry in the encoding; every other word is already absorbed as a suffix of a longer one already counted. Summing (length + 1) for each such leaf-ending word gives the shortest total length, since deduplication also naturally happens: if two words are identical the trie only stores it once, but since input words are distinct, this doesn't reduce further.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(sum of word lengths) for the trie
